plannedCharts.title: India keeps slipping down the water ladder
plannedCharts.unit: cubic metres per person per year
plannedCharts.subtitle: CWC Reassessment of Water Availability, 2019 · average annual per-capita water availability
plannedCharts.whyThisChart: The simplest measure of stress: how much water there is to go round, per person, as the population keeps growing.

plannedCharts.title: How much of India's water can actually be used
plannedCharts.subtitle: CWC water-resource estimation · total resource vs usable surface and groundwater
plannedCharts.whyThisChart: The headline 'India has 1,999 BCM of water' is misleading - most of it cannot be captured and used.

plannedCharts.title: Nationally, India pumps about 60% of what refills each year
plannedCharts.subtitle: CGWB Dynamic Ground Water Resource Assessment · national stage of extraction, 2020-2025
plannedCharts.whyThisChart: The single number officials cite to say groundwater is 'under control' - and the one that hides the most.

plannedCharts.title: Most blocks are safe - but one in nine is over-exploited
plannedCharts.subtitle: CGWB 2025 assessment · 6,762 assessment units by category
plannedCharts.whyThisChart: Breaking the country into thousands of small assessment units shows the damage the national average buries.

plannedCharts.title: The crisis has an address: the north-west
plannedCharts.subtitle: CGWB 2025 assessment · stage of groundwater extraction by state
plannedCharts.whyThisChart: Put extraction on a map and the abstract 60% average resolves into a sharp regional emergency.

plannedCharts.title: A calm national line, three states in free fall
plannedCharts.subtitle: CGWB assessments 2020-2025 · stage of extraction, national vs the north-west belt
plannedCharts.whyThisChart: The honest test of the 'groundwater is improving' story: hold the national line against the worst states.

plannedCharts.title: Where India's water actually goes
plannedCharts.subtitle: World Bank / FAO AQUASTAT · freshwater withdrawal by sector (latest available)
plannedCharts.whyThisChart: Before blaming taps and showers, see who the big user really is.

plannedCharts.title: India earns very little per drop
plannedCharts.subtitle: World Bank · water productivity (GDP per cubic metre of freshwater withdrawn)
plannedCharts.whyThisChart: Water stress is also an efficiency story: how much economic value India wrings from each unit of water.

plannedCharts.title: The water that is left is often unsafe
plannedCharts.unit: % of tested samples above the safe limit
plannedCharts.subtitle: CGWB Annual Ground Water Quality Report 2024 · 15,259 monitoring sites
plannedCharts.whyThisChart: Depletion is only half the problem - what remains is increasingly contaminated.

plannedCharts.title: Contamination reaches into hundreds of districts
plannedCharts.subtitle: CGWB 2024 report (Year-2023 data) · districts with groundwater contamination
plannedCharts.whyThisChart: Quality problems are not a few isolated villages - they are spread across much of the country.

plannedCharts.title: Tap water reached most of rural India in five years
plannedCharts.subtitle: Jal Jeevan Mission · rural households with a tap-water connection
plannedCharts.whyThisChart: The state's biggest recent water success, and the human counterpoint to the depletion story.

plannedCharts.title: Safe drinking water finally reaches most homes
plannedCharts.subtitle: World Bank / WHO-UNICEF JMP · population using safely managed drinking water
plannedCharts.whyThisChart: The genuine good-news counterpoint: access has improved markedly.

plannedCharts.title: More taps, less water: the paradox in one frame
plannedCharts.subtitle: World Bank · drinking-water access vs renewable freshwater per person
plannedCharts.whyThisChart: The article's thesis: India is getting better at delivering water to people while the resource itself shrinks.

selectionRules: Start from the page question, not from the indicator name.
Choose the smallest set of visuals that explains scale, trend, structure, comparison, and caveat.
Prefer mobile-friendly charts: line charts with sparse ticks, horizontal bars, share strips, pyramids only when essential, and no dense tables.
Use one strong pull quote only when the evidence supports it with a number.
Add glossary blocks for technical terms that normal readers may not know.
caveats: Use only figures present in lockedNumbers or sourceSummaries.
If a related theme indicator is present, you may use it for context, but do not pretend it is the main answer.
If source coverage is thin, say so directly.
Do not compare states, districts, or cities unless the evidence packet contains those geographies.
forbiddenClaims: Do not infer causality from a trend unless the evidence explicitly supports it.
Do not cite a source that is not present in sourceSummaries.
